events.continuity_hook: Flights and lodging are booked, and the final work location now allows the Friday ground plan to be completed.
events.interaction_goal: Verify the hotel-to-annex trip, confirm post-checkout luggage handling, and set a museum departure time that protects the booked flight.
events.scenario_brief: The receiving museum confirms that Friday’s unpacking will take place in the annex several blocks from the main building. Avery’s two-night hotel reservation remains suitable, but she needs to check the morning route to the annex, arrange luggage storage after checkout, and preserve enough time for the booked Friday evening flight.

events.continuity_hook: The work dates and approximate daily commitments are known, while the arrival day, return day, and lodging span remain unsettled.
events.interaction_goal: Compare workable round-trip schedules, account for airport-to-museum travel, and determine whether the assignment requires two or three hotel nights.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to oversee a Baltimore exhibition deinstallation on Tuesday and Wednesday. She must initially report by 9:00 a.m. Tuesday, the final crate is expected to leave around 5:00 p.m. Wednesday, and she is weighing a Monday evening flight against an early Tuesday departure as well as a Wednesday night return against one more hotel night.

events.continuity_hook: Monday arrival and at least two hotel nights are now fixed, but the exact outbound and return pairing still needs to be selected.
events.interaction_goal: Book the Monday flight and choose a Wednesday return only if the post-deinstallation airport margin is realistic; otherwise retain Thursday as the return option.
events.scenario_brief: The museum moves Tuesday’s reporting time to 7:30 a.m., eliminating the same-day outbound. A Monday evening nonstop is available, while two Wednesday return flights differ in how much time they allow after the planned 5:00 p.m. crate departure and the trip to the airport.

events.continuity_hook: Air travel and hotel dates are settled, leaving lodging cost, daily access, and rate terms to resolve.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete three-night charges and practical morning routes, select the appropriate rate, and reserve the hotel.
events.scenario_brief: Avery has booked a Monday outbound and a Thursday morning return, creating a three-night stay. The leading hotel is walkable to the museum but charges separately for breakfast, while a less expensive property requires a short transit trip and has an earlier cancellation deadline; both show availability for the full stay.

events.continuity_hook: The assignment now extends into Thursday, requiring coordinated changes to the return flight and hotel checkout.
events.interaction_goal: Find a viable Thursday evening or Friday return, compare any fare difference, extend the hotel only as needed, and produce the updated itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: The outgoing carrier delays the final crate pickup until 7:30 p.m. Wednesday and asks Avery to witness a seal inspection early Thursday. Her Thursday morning flight is now too early, and the reserved hotel can add Thursday night at the original nightly rate if amended before the next day.

events.continuity_hook: The weekend and purpose are established, while the travel mode, arrival time, Sunday return, and two-night hotel remain unchosen.
events.interaction_goal: Compare realistic door-to-door timing for flying and driving, identify workable Friday and Sunday schedules, and establish the area and dates for a shared hotel stay.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife plan a Friday-to-Sunday visit to relatives in Raleigh and will share one hotel room. They need to arrive before a Saturday morning family gathering, but Friday work obligations make both an evening flight and a drive after work plausible; Sunday departure timing remains open around a late lunch.
